brief: lead's message, 2026-11-22: JS-168's merge-queue run failed on its own regression
tradeoff: With the room rule gone, a helper is claimed by the viewers' own worker when it has the cores: one worker and two viewers of one spec run two jobs where main runs one, and about ten older checks fail
serves: JS-168 criterion 6: 'with one worker nothing changes'. PRODUCT.md: 'A heavy film uses the whole cluster's processors rather than stalling on one machine while others sit idle.'
entry: A helper is never claimed by a worker that is running a viewer's, a seek's or a failover's job of its spec, and with one worker no helper is queued or claimed whatever its free cores; a worker running only helpers of the spec may still take another after the one-second wait when it has the cores. JS-168 criterion 6 is made exact so, the older checks stand unamended but for one subcase (D-053), and docs/transcoding.md and DOMAINS.md invariant 58 state the rule. Rejected: allowing same-worker helpers (C: ten checks amended for a speed-up nobody measured); measuring first (D: holds a merge for an answer that would not change what lands); forbidding every second job of a spec on a worker (A: could take a large worker's second helper, unverified whether the 2+6 runs used one). Given up: the same-worker helper a lone worker with room for three jobs got before JS-168, read from the old code and never measured, by nobody known. Unverified when decided: whether a same-worker helper speeds a slow job on a worker with idle cores; whether any JS-168 long run had a helper beside a viewer's job on one worker (such a row is run again, holding nothing). Data that reopens it: a measurement of a same-worker helper reaching 1.0x on idle cores; the dogfood showing a job under 1.2x on a worker with the job's cost free and no other worker to help.
